title: Extend `st.chat_input` to support embedded controls (buttons, dropdowns, toggles, etc.)
body:
### Checklist - [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests. - [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue. ### Summary Currently, `st.chat_input` provides a clean and simple text + audio + attachments input experience, which is great for basic chat use cases. However, for more advanced AI-driven applications, this component feels limiting compared to modern AI chat interfaces. Many AI chat products (e.g. ChatGPT, VS Code Copilot Chat, etc.) allow users to configure options at the moment of sending a message, such as: - Selecting the model to use - Enabling/disabling web search or retrieval - Activating deep research / reasoning modes - Toggling custom features (tools, plugins, etc.) _Examples:_
## ✅ Proposed improvement - Extend st.chat_input to support embedded UI components, such as: - Dropdowns - Toggles / Checkboxes - Buttons - And more ### Why? ## ❌ Current limitations With Streamlit today: - These options must be placed outside the chat input, like sidebar - This breaks the conversational UX and feels disconnected from the message being sent ### How? _No response_ ### Additional Context _No response_
